title: Verb 'To Be' (Identity & State) 👤
rule: The verb 'to be' connects a subject to a name, identity, or state. [Subject] + [am/is/are] + [Name/Noun].

examples.text: I am James.

targetLang.en: I am James.
targetLang.fr: Je suis James.
targetLang.es: Yo soy James.
targetLang.it: Io sono James.
targetLang.de: Ich bin James.
targetLang.ru: Я Джеймс.

examples.context: Introducing yourself to someone.

interactiveExercises.question: Choose the correct form: 'I ___ a teacher.'
interactiveExercises.explanation: Use 'am' with 'I'.

dialogues.prompt: Hello! I am James York.

title: Personal Pronouns (I / You / He / She) 👥
rule: Personal pronouns replace specific nouns to refer to speakers, listeners, or others. Example: 'I', 'You'.

examples.text: I am a friend. You are a teacher.

targetLang.en: I am a friend. You are a teacher.
targetLang.fr: Je suis un ami. Tu es un professeur.
targetLang.es: Yo soy un amigo. Tú eres un maestro.
targetLang.it: Io sono un amico. Tu sei un insegnante.
targetLang.de: Ich bin ein Freund. Du bist ein Lehrer.
targetLang.ru: Я друг. Ты учитель.

examples.context: Identifying participants in dialogue.

interactiveExercises.question: Which pronoun refers to yourself?
interactiveExercises.explanation: 'I' is the first-person singular pronoun.

dialogues.prompt: I am the receptionist. Who are you?

title: Demonstrative 'This is' 👈
rule: Use 'This is' to introduce people, places, or objects close to you. [This is] + [a/an/my] + [Noun].

examples.text: This is COSYlanguages Headquarters.

targetLang.en: This is COSYlanguages Headquarters.
targetLang.fr: C'est le siège de COSYlanguages.
targetLang.es: Esta es la sede de COSYlanguages.
targetLang.it: Questa è la sede di COSYlanguages.
targetLang.de: Das ist die COSYlanguages-Zentrale.
targetLang.ru: Это штаб-квартира COSYlanguages.

examples.context: Introducing a location.

interactiveExercises.question: How do you introduce your friend?
interactiveExercises.explanation: Use 'This is' for singular introductions.

dialogues.prompt: This is the reception desk!

title: Possessive Adjectives (My / Your) 🔑
rule: Possessives show ownership or relationship. [My/Your] + [Noun]. Example: 'My name', 'Your key'.

examples.text: Here is your key.

targetLang.en: Here is your key.
targetLang.fr: Voici votre clé.
targetLang.es: Aquí está tu llave.
targetLang.it: Ecco la tua chiave.
targetLang.de: Hier ist Ihr Schlüssel.
targetLang.ru: Вот ваш ключ.

examples.context: Handing an item to someone.

interactiveExercises.question: Complete the sentence: 'What is ___ name?'
interactiveExercises.explanation: Use 'your' when asking someone about their name.

dialogues.prompt: Here is your key for your new apartment!

title: Indefinite Articles (A / An) 🚪
rule: Use 'a' before consonant sounds and 'an' before vowel sounds for singular countable nouns. [a/an] + [Noun].

examples.text: This is a key. This is an apartment.

targetLang.en: This is a key. This is an apartment.
targetLang.fr: C'est une clé. C'est un appartement.
targetLang.es: Esta es una llave. Este es un apartamento.
targetLang.it: Questa è una chiave. Questo è un appartamento.
targetLang.de: Das ist ein Schlüssel. Das ist eine Wohnung.
targetLang.ru: Это ключ. Это квартира.

examples.context: Describing objects and places.

interactiveExercises.question: Which is correct before 'apartment'?
interactiveExercises.explanation: 'Apartment' starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.

dialogues.prompt: This is a door to an apartment!

title: Greetings & Imperative Actions 👋
rule: Imperative Actions: Use base verb forms directly to express direct actions or commands ([Verb] + [Object]). Example: 'Open the door'. Greetings combine an opening word with an action.

examples.text: 👋 Hello, open the door!

targetLang.en: 👋 Hello, open the door!
targetLang.fr: 👋 Bonjour, ouvrez la porte !
targetLang.es: 👋 ¡Hola, abre la puerta!
targetLang.it: 👋 Ciao, apri la porta!
targetLang.de: 👋 Hallo, öffne die Tür!
targetLang.ru: 👋 Здравствуйте, откройте дверь!

examples.context: Greeting an NPC and taking immediate action on an object.

examples.text: 🔑 Take the key and open the door.

targetLang.en: 🔑 Take the key and open the door.
targetLang.fr: 🔑 Prenez la clé et ouvrez la porte.
targetLang.es: 🔑 Toma la llave y abre la puerta.
targetLang.it: 🔑 Prendi la chiave e apri la porta!
targetLang.de: 🔑 Nimm den Schlüssel und öffne die Tür.
targetLang.ru: 🔑 Возьмите ключ и откройте дверь.

examples.context: Executing direct action sequences in cause-and-effect chains.

interactiveExercises.question: Which imperative phrase tells someone to unlock the entrance?
interactiveExercises.explanation: Imperative verbs start with the base form of the verb without suffixes.

interactiveExercises.question: Reorder words to form a polite imperative greeting:
interactiveExercises.explanation: Start with greeting, followed by base verb and direct object.

dialogues.prompt: 👋 Look! 👉 Key ➔ Door ➔ Open!
dialogues.grammarUsage: Imperative direct command used in living room tutorial.

title: Existential Placement & Identification (There is) 🛋️
rule: Use 'There is' (+ singular noun) to point out the presence of one item. Pattern: [There is] + [a/an] + [Noun].

examples.text: There is a sofa in the living room.

targetLang.en: There is a sofa in the living room.
targetLang.fr: Il y a un canapé dans le salon.
targetLang.es: Hay un sofá en el salón.
targetLang.it: C'è un divano nel salotto.
targetLang.de: Es gibt ein Sofa im Wohnzimmer.
targetLang.ru: В гостиной есть диван.

examples.context: Describing rooms and furniture.

interactiveExercises.question: Choose the correct phrase to identify one object:
options: There is a key on the table
There are a key on table
interactiveExercises.explanation: Use 'There is' for singular items.

dialogues.prompt: There is a lamp in the living room!
dialogues.grammarUsage: Pointing out singular objects in a room.

title: Plural Existential Placement (There are) 📚
rule: Use 'There are' (+ plural noun/number) to point out multiple items. Pattern: [There are] + [Number/Plural Noun].

examples.text: There are three cups in the kitchen.

targetLang.en: There are three cups in the kitchen.
targetLang.fr: Il y a trois tasses dans la cuisine.
targetLang.es: Hay tres tazas en la cocina.
targetLang.it: Ci sono tre tazze in cucina.
targetLang.de: Es gibt drei Tassen in der Küche.
targetLang.ru: На кухне есть три чашки.

examples.context: Counting and pointing out plural objects.

interactiveExercises.question: How do you state the presence of multiple chairs?
interactiveExercises.explanation: Use 'There are' with plural nouns.

dialogues.prompt: There are two lamps in the bedroom!
dialogues.grammarUsage: Stating plural objects in a room.

title: Demonstrative Pronoun 'This' 👈
rule: Use 'This' for a singular item close to the speaker. Pattern: [This] + [is] + [a/an/my] + [Noun].

examples.text: This is my desk.

targetLang.en: This is my desk.
targetLang.fr: C'est mon bureau.
targetLang.es: Este es mi escritorio.
targetLang.it: Questa è la mia scrivania.
targetLang.de: Das ist mein Schreibtisch.
targetLang.ru: Это мой письменный стол.

examples.context: Pointing out nearby objects.

interactiveExercises.question: Which word identifies a nearby item?
interactiveExercises.explanation: 'This' refers to singular nearby items.

dialogues.prompt: This is a red sofa!

title: Demonstrative Pronoun 'That' 👉
rule: Use 'That' for a singular item at a distance. Pattern: [That] + [is] + [a/an/your] + [Noun].

examples.text: That is a blue bed.

targetLang.en: That is a blue bed.
targetLang.fr: C'est un lit bleu.
targetLang.es: Esa es una cama azul.
targetLang.it: Quello è un letto blu.
targetLang.de: Das ist ein blaues Bett.
targetLang.ru: То синяя кровать.

examples.context: Pointing out distant items.

interactiveExercises.question: Which word points to an object further away?
interactiveExercises.explanation: 'That' refers to singular distant objects.

dialogues.prompt: That is the balcony over there!

title: Daily Actions & Habitual Routines (Present Simple) 🏃
rule: Present Simple Tense: Used for habitual routines and direct current states. Structure: [Subject] + [Base Verb]. Example: 'I wake up at seven o'clock'.

examples.text: I wake up and brush my teeth every morning.

targetLang.en: I wake up and brush my teeth every morning.
targetLang.fr: Je me réveille et me brosse les dents chaque matin.
targetLang.es: Me despierto y me cepillo los dientes cada mañana.
targetLang.it: Mi sveglio e mi lavo i denti ogni mattina.
targetLang.de: Ich wache auf und putze mir jeden Morgen die Zähne.
targetLang.ru: Я просыпаюсь и чищу зубы каждое утро.

examples.context: Describing morning routine.

interactiveExercises.question: Which sentence correctly describes a morning habit?
options: I wake up at seven o'clock
I wakes up at seven o'clock
interactiveExercises.explanation: First person singular 'I' uses base verb form.

dialogues.prompt: I wake up early and study every morning!

title: Telling Time & Time of Day 🕒
rule: Use 'at [time]' and time of day expressions: 'in the morning', 'in the afternoon', 'in the evening'. Pattern: [at + time] / [in the + time_of_day].

examples.text: What time is it? It is eight o'clock in the morning.

targetLang.en: What time is it? It is eight o'clock in the morning.
targetLang.fr: Quelle heure est-il ? Il est huit heures du matin.
targetLang.es: ¿Qué hora es? Son las ocho de la mañana.
targetLang.it: Che ora è? Sono le otto del mattino.
targetLang.de: Wie spät ist es? Es ist acht Uhr morgens.
targetLang.ru: Который час? Восемь часов утра.

examples.context: Asking and telling time.

interactiveExercises.question: How do you ask someone the current time?
interactiveExercises.explanation: Use 'What time is it?' to ask the time.

dialogues.prompt: It is eight o'clock in the morning! Time for breakfast!
dialogues.grammarUsage: Stating current time and period of day.

title: Adverbs of Frequency (Always / Usually / Never) 🔄
rule: Place frequency adverbs before main verbs or after 'to be'. Pattern: [Subject] + [always/usually/sometimes/never] + [Verb].

examples.text: I always brush my teeth in the morning. I am never late.

targetLang.en: I always brush my teeth in the morning. I am never late.
targetLang.fr: Je me brosse toujours les dents le matin. Je ne suis jamais en retard.
targetLang.es: Siempre me cepillo los dientes por la mañana. Nunca llego tarde.
targetLang.it: Lavo sempre i denti la mattina. Non sono mai in ritardo.
targetLang.de: Ich putze mir morgens immer die Zähne. Ich bin nie zu spät.
targetLang.ru: Я всегда чищу зубы по утрам. Я никогда не опаздываю.

examples.context: Expressing frequency of habits.

interactiveExercises.question: Which word means 100% of the time?
interactiveExercises.explanation: 'Always' expresses 100% frequency.

dialogues.prompt: I always take the bus at eight o'clock!

title: Preferences & Requests ❤️
rule: Expressing Desires and Preferences: Use 'I like [Noun]' for general preference and 'I would like [Noun]' or 'I want [Noun]' for polite orders. Pattern: [Subject] + [Verb of Preference] + [Object].

examples.text: 🥖 I like fresh warm baguette from the bakery.

targetLang.en: 🥖 I like fresh warm baguette from the bakery.
targetLang.fr: 🥖 J'aime la baguette fraîche de la boulangerie.
targetLang.es: 🥖 Me gusta la baguette fresca de la panadería.
targetLang.it: 🥖 Mi piace la baguette fresca della panetteria.
targetLang.de: 🥖 Ich mag frisches warmes Baguette aus der Bäckerei.
targetLang.ru: 🥖 Мне нравится свежий теплый багет из пекарни.

examples.context: Expressing food preferences in shop contexts.

examples.text: ☕ I want a hot espresso, please.

targetLang.en: ☕ I want a hot espresso, please.
targetLang.fr: ☕ Je voudrais un café chaud, s'il vous plaît.
targetLang.es: ☕ Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
targetLang.it: ☕ Vorrei un caffè caldo, per favore.
targetLang.de: ☕ Ich hätte gerne einen heißen Espresso, bitte.
targetLang.ru: ☕ Я бы хотел горячий эспрессо, пожалуйста.

examples.context: Ordering drinks politely at the cafe.

interactiveExercises.question: How do you express a preference for bakery bread?
interactiveExercises.explanation: First-person 'I' takes 'like' in the present tense.

dialogues.prompt: 🥖 Warm baguette! 😋 Do you like fresh bread?

title: Spatial Prepositions (next to / behind / between) 📍
rule: Use prepositions to describe relative positions of places and objects: next to, behind, between, in front of. Pattern: [Subject] + [is/are] + [preposition] + [the + Object].

examples.text: The bakery is next to the cafe. The bus stop is in front of the street.

targetLang.en: The bakery is next to the cafe. The bus stop is in front of the street.
targetLang.fr: La boulangerie est à côté du café. L'arrêt de bus est devant la rue.
targetLang.es: La panadería está al lado del café. La parada de autobús está delante de la calle.
targetLang.it: La panetteria è accanto al caffè. La fermata dell'autobus è davanti alla strada.
targetLang.de: Die Bäckerei ist neben dem Café. Die Bushaltestelle ist vor der Straße.
targetLang.ru: Пекарня находится рядом с кафе. Автобусная остановка перед улицей.

examples.context: Describing town locations relative to each other.

interactiveExercises.question: Which preposition means 'beside' or 'at the side of'?
interactiveExercises.explanation: 'Next to' indicates position directly adjacent or beside an item.

dialogues.prompt: The bakery is next to the cafe in Town Square!

title: Directional Imperatives (go / come / turn) 🧭
rule: Directional imperatives use base verbs to give directions: 'Go straight', 'Turn left', 'Turn right', 'Come here'. Pattern: [Base Verb] + [Direction].

examples.text: Go straight and turn left at the bakery.

targetLang.en: Go straight and turn left at the bakery.
targetLang.fr: Allez tout droit et tournez à gauche à la boulangerie.
targetLang.es: Sigue recto y gira a la izquierda en la panadería.
targetLang.it: Vai dritto e gira a sinistra alla panetteria.
targetLang.de: Gehen Sie geradeaus und biegen Sie an der Bäckerei links ab.
targetLang.ru: Идите прямо и поверните налево у пекарни.

examples.context: Giving and following directions in town.

interactiveExercises.question: Which verb phrase tells someone to change direction left?
interactiveExercises.explanation: 'Turn left' directs someone to pivot leftward.

dialogues.prompt: Turn right at the street clock to find the bus stop!

title: Countable & Uncountable Nouns 🛒
rule: Countable nouns can be counted individually (apple -> apples). Uncountable nouns refer to substances or concepts (bread, water, milk, sugar). Pattern: [a/an/numbers + Countable Noun] vs [Uncountable Noun].

examples.text: I buy two apples and fresh bread.

targetLang.en: I buy two apples and fresh bread.
targetLang.fr: J'achète deux pommes et du pain frais.
targetLang.es: Compro dos manzanas y pan fresco.
targetLang.it: Compro due mele e pane fresco.
targetLang.de: Ich kaufe zwei Äpfel und frisches Brot.
targetLang.ru: Я покупаю два яблока и свежий хлеб.

examples.context: Shopping for countable and uncountable groceries.

interactiveExercises.question: Which item is an uncountable noun?
interactiveExercises.explanation: 'Bread' is uncountable; individual loaves or baguettes are counted.

dialogues.prompt: We sell individual baguettes and fresh flour!

title: Quantifiers 'Some' & 'Any' 🥖
rule: Use 'some' in positive statements with plural or uncountable nouns. Use 'any' in questions and negative statements. Pattern: [Subject + Verb + some + Noun] vs [Do you have any + Noun?].

examples.text: I have some fresh apples. Do you have any tea?

targetLang.en: I have some fresh apples. Do you have any tea?
targetLang.fr: J'ai des pommes fraîches. Avez-vous du thé ?
targetLang.es: Tengo algunas manzanas frescas. ¿Tienes té?
targetLang.it: Ho alcune mele fresche. Hai del tè?
targetLang.de: Ich habe einige frische Äpfel. Haben Sie Tee?
targetLang.ru: У меня есть немного свежих яблок. У вас есть чай?

examples.context: Offering and asking for quantities.

interactiveExercises.question: Which word fills the gap in a question: 'Do you have ___ water?'
interactiveExercises.explanation: Use 'any' in questions asking about availability.

dialogues.prompt: Would you like some warm milk with your espresso?

title: Asking Quantities ('How much' / 'How many') 💰
rule: Use 'How many' with plural countable nouns. Use 'How much' with uncountable nouns or when asking prices. Pattern: [How many + Countable Plural] vs [How much + Uncountable / price].

examples.text: How many baguettes do you want? How much is the coffee?

targetLang.en: How many baguettes do you want? How much is the coffee?
targetLang.fr: Combien de baguettes voulez-vous ? Combien coûte le café ?
targetLang.es: ¿Cuántas baguettes quieres? ¿Cuánto cuesta el café?
targetLang.it: Quante baguette vuoi? Quanto costa il caffè?
targetLang.de: Wie viele Baguettes möchten Sie? Wie viel kostet der Kaffee?
targetLang.ru: Сколько багетов вы хотите? Сколько стоит кофе?

examples.context: Inquiring about quantities and prices when shopping.

interactiveExercises.question: Which phrase asks about the cost of an item?
interactiveExercises.explanation: Use 'How much' to ask for prices.

dialogues.prompt: How many loaves of bread would you like today?

title: Modal Verbs 'Can' & 'Can't' (Ability & Permission) 🏫
rule: Use 'can' for ability or permission and 'can't' (cannot) for inability or prohibition. Pattern: [Subject] + [can / can't] + [Base Verb].

examples.text: I can speak English. You can study in the library.

targetLang.en: I can speak English. You can study in the library.
targetLang.fr: Je peux parler anglais. Vous pouvez étudier à la bibliothèque.
targetLang.es: Puedo hablar inglés. Puedes estudiar en la biblioteca.
targetLang.it: Posso parlare inglese. Puoi studiare in biblioteca.
targetLang.de: Ich kann Englisch sprechen. Du kannst in der Bibliothek lernen.
targetLang.ru: Я могу говорить по-английски. Вы можете заниматься в библиотеке.

examples.context: Expressing language skills and allowed activities at school.

interactiveExercises.question: Complete the ability sentence: 'She ___ read French books.'
interactiveExercises.explanation: Modal verb 'can' does not change form for third-person singular.

dialogues.prompt: You can practice pronunciation with me in the language classroom!

title: Past Simple Tense (Completed Past Actions) 📜
rule: Use Past Simple to describe completed actions at a definite time in the past. Regular verbs add -ed (visited, walked). Irregular verbs change form (went, came, saw). Pattern: [Subject] + [Past Verb].

examples.text: I visited the town hall yesterday. James came to COSY Town.

targetLang.en: I visited the town hall yesterday. James came to COSY Town.
targetLang.fr: J'ai visité l'hôtel de ville hier. James est venu à COSY Town.
targetLang.es: Visité el ayuntamiento ayer. James vino a COSY Town.
targetLang.it: Ho visitato il municipio ieri. James è venuto a COSY Town.
targetLang.de: Ich habe gestern das Rathaus besucht. James kam nach COSY Town.
targetLang.ru: Я посетил ратушу вчера. Джеймс приехал в COSY Town.

examples.context: Sharing historic events and recent activities.

interactiveExercises.question: What is the past simple form of 'visit'?
interactiveExercises.explanation: Regular past simple verbs take the suffix '-ed'.

dialogues.prompt: I traveled across many cities before arriving in COSY Town!

title: Past Time Expressions (yesterday / last / ago) ⏳
rule: Time expressions specify when past actions occurred: 'yesterday', 'last week / month', '[time] ago'. Pattern: [Past Simple Clause] + [Time Expression].

examples.text: I saw the exhibit two days ago. We met last week.

targetLang.en: I saw the exhibit two days ago. We met last week.
targetLang.fr: J'ai vu l'exposition il y a deux jours. Nous nous sommes rencontrés la semaine dernière.
targetLang.es: Vi la exposición hace dos días. Nos conocimos la semana pasada.
targetLang.it: Ho visto la mostra due giorni fa. Ci siamo incontrati la settimana scorsa.
targetLang.de: Ich habe die Ausstellung vor zwei Tagen gesehen. Wir haben uns letzte Woche getroffen.
targetLang.ru: Я видел выставку два дня назад. Мы встретились на прошлой неделе.

examples.context: Specifying precise timing of completed actions.

interactiveExercises.question: Which time word completes: 'I walked in the park two hours ___'?
interactiveExercises.explanation: Use 'ago' after a duration of time to indicate how far in the past it occurred.

dialogues.prompt: I completed the vocabulary challenge three days ago!

title: Comparative Adjectives (-er / more) ⚖️
rule: Compare two items using '-er than' for short adjectives (bigger than, taller than) and 'more ... than' for longer adjectives (more famous than). Pattern: [Noun A] + [is] + [Adj-er / more Adj] + [than] + [Noun B].

examples.text: The park is bigger than the garden. The museum is more famous than the cafe.

targetLang.en: The park is bigger than the garden. The museum is more famous than the cafe.
targetLang.fr: Le parc est plus grand que le jardin. Le musée est plus célèbre que le café.
targetLang.es: El parque es más grande que el jardín. El museo es más famoso que el café.
targetLang.it: Il parco è più grande del giardino. Il museo è più famoso del caffè.
targetLang.de: Der Park ist größer als der Garten. Das Museum ist berühmter als das Café.
targetLang.ru: Парк больше, чем сад. Музей более знаменит, чем кафе.

examples.context: Comparing places and focal points in the community park area.

interactiveExercises.question: Which sentence correctly compares two sizes?
options: The park is bigger than the square
The park is more big than square
The park is big than square
interactiveExercises.explanation: Short adjectives like 'big' take the '-er' suffix in comparatives (bigger).

dialogues.prompt: The community garden is greener than the town square!

title: Possession Expression ('Have Got') 🎒
rule: Use 'have got' / 'has got' to express possession or attributes in informal communication. Pattern: [Subject] + [have got / has got] + [Noun]. Negative: haven't got / hasn't got.

examples.text: I have got a green backpack. She has got a map.

targetLang.en: I have got a green backpack. She has got a map.
targetLang.fr: J'ai un sac à dos vert. Elle a une carte.
targetLang.es: Tengo una mochila verde. Ella tiene un mapa.
targetLang.it: Ho uno zaino verde. Lei ha una mappa.
targetLang.de: Ich habe einen grünen Rucksack. Sie hat eine Karte.
targetLang.ru: У меня есть зеленый рюкзак. У нее есть карта.

examples.context: Discussing personal items and personal belongings.

interactiveExercises.question: Choose the correct phrase: 'He ___ a new key.'
interactiveExercises.explanation: Third-person singular 'He' takes 'has got'.

dialogues.prompt: I have got many language flashcards in my apartment!

title: Verbs 'Need' & 'Feel' (Needs & Feelings) 💭
rule: Use 'need' (+ Noun / Infinitive) to express requirements and 'feel' (+ Adjective) to express emotional or physical states. Pattern: [I need + Noun] / [I feel + Adjective].

examples.text: I need a rest. I feel happy today.

targetLang.en: I need a rest. I feel happy today.
targetLang.fr: J'ai besoin de repos. Je me sens heureux aujourd'hui.
targetLang.es: Necesito un descanso. Me siento feliz hoy.
targetLang.it: Ho bisogno di riposo. Mi sento felice oggi.
targetLang.de: Ich brauche eine Pause. Ich fühle mich heute glücklich.
targetLang.ru: Мне нужен отдых. Я чувствую себя счастливым сегодня.

examples.context: Expressing internal states and needs in social settings.

interactiveExercises.question: Complete the sentence: 'I ___ tired after walking through town.'
interactiveExercises.explanation: Use 'feel' before adjectives describing personal state.

dialogues.prompt: I feel excited about exploring the park!

title: Present Continuous Tense (Action in Progress) 🔄
rule: Use Present Continuous to describe actions happening right now at the time of speaking. Pattern: [Subject] + [am/is/are] + [Verb-ing]. Example: 'I am drinking coffee', 'She is walking in the park'.

examples.text: I am drinking coffee with Ella. She is talking to her friend.

targetLang.en: I am drinking coffee with Ella. She is talking to her friend.
targetLang.fr: Je bois du café avec Ella. Elle parle à son amie.
targetLang.es: Estoy bebiendo café con Ella. Ella está hablando con su amiga.
targetLang.it: Sto bevendo un caffè con Ella. Sta parlando con la sua amica.
targetLang.de: Ich trinke Kaffee mit Ella. Sie spricht mit ihrer Freundin.
targetLang.ru: Я пью кофе с Эллой. Она разговаривает со своей подругой.

examples.context: Describing active conversations and current actions.

interactiveExercises.question: Choose the correct present continuous form: 'He ___ in the park right now.'
interactiveExercises.explanation: Use 'is' + verb-ing for third-person continuous action happening now.

dialogues.prompt: I am practicing English pronunciation right now!

title: Expressing Future Plans ('Going to') ✈️
rule: Use 'be going to' + base verb to express planned future intentions or travel predictions. Pattern: [Subject] + [am/is/are] + [going to] + [Base Verb].

examples.text: I am going to travel to the airport tomorrow.

targetLang.en: I am going to travel to the airport tomorrow.
targetLang.fr: Je vais voyager à l'aéroport demain.
targetLang.es: Voy a viajar al aeropuerto mañana.
targetLang.it: Sto per viaggiare all'aeroporto domani.
targetLang.de: Ich werde morgen zum Flughafen reisen.
targetLang.ru: Я собираюсь поехать в аэропорт завтра.

examples.context: Planning travel and future explorations.

interactiveExercises.question: Which sentence expresses a future intention?
options: I am going to visit the hotel
interactiveExercises.explanation: Structure [am/is/are + going to + verb] expresses future intentions.

dialogues.prompt: I am going to visit the tourist office next!
